extracted.intended_audience: prospective Knight-Hennessy Scholars applicants (students planning to apply to Stanford graduate programs)
extracted.subtask_description: Official eligibility rules for applying to the Knight-Hennessy Scholars program (cohort-specific; page shows requirements for the 2027 cohort), including baseline requirements, program exclusions, degree date windows, special cases (military, undocumented, current Stanford students), and fellowship-combination rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: No categorical restrictions (age/field/affiliation/region)
rubrics_metrics.description: Knight-Hennessy Scholars has no restrictions based on age, college or university, field of study, or career aspiration. We encourage citizens and residents of all countries to apply. We do not require applicants to seek endorsements from colleges, universities, or other institutions. Additionally, we have no quotas by discipline, program, or world region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an inclusive statement: applicants should not be deterred by age, institutional affiliation, discipline, or geography; endorsements are not required; selection is not quota-driven by region/discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline Requirement 1: Admission to Stanford (must be met)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to applying to Knight-Hennessy Scholars, you must apply to, be accepted by, and enroll in a full-time Stanford graduate degree program (examples: DMA, JD, MA, MBA, MD, MFA, MPP, MS, PhD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must also satisfy at least one of the four listed eligibility pathways (see separate metrics for each pathway). The requirement focuses on enrollment in a full-time Stanford graduate degree program aligned with your KHS enrollment year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility pathway A: Applying separately but concurrently
rubrics_metrics.description: You are applying separately but concurrently to KHS and a full-time Stanford graduate degree program such that you will start both in the same year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concurrent application means you plan to enroll in both the Stanford program and KHS in the same academic year (the cohort year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility pathway B: Already offered and deferred admission
rubrics_metrics.description: You have already been offered and deferred admission to a full-time Stanford graduate degree program, and will apply to KHS such that you will start both in the same year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a deferred admission to Stanford, you may apply to KHS for the year you will enroll, provided all other eligibility conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility pathway C: Current Stanford graduate student adding a new full-time program
rubrics_metrics.description: You are a current Stanford graduate student who will apply to add a new full-time Stanford graduate degree program, such that you will start both KHS and the new program in the same year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current students must be adding a different full-time degree program (not a coterminal or same-discipline MA/MS addition) and plan to start the new program in the cohort year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility pathway D: Current Stanford PhD student in first year
rubrics_metrics.description: You are a current Stanford PhD student in your first year of enrollment, and will apply to KHS such that you will start KHS in your second year of PhD enrollment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This pathway applies only to PhD students in their first year; the intended KHS start aligns with the second year of PhD enrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible Stanford graduate degree programs / program exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The following Stanford graduate degree programs are not eligible for Knight-Hennessy Scholars: Honors Cooperative Program; Master of Liberal Arts; Doctor of Science of Law (JSD) and the Master of Legal Studies (MLS); current Stanford PhD students adding an MA or MS degree in their PhD discipline; coterminal degrees (current Stanford students enrolled in a coterminal degree must be applying to a different full-time Stanford degree program to apply for Knight-Hennessy Scholars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your Stanford degree program is listed here or falls into these categories (coterminal, same-discipline MA/MS added to PhD), you are not eligible for KHS under that program. Check program-specific eligibility before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline Requirement 2: Undergraduate degree date (recency window)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must have earned, in January 2020 or later, a U.S. bachelor’s degree or its equivalent from a college or university of recognized standing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the 2027 cohort: you must have earned your first bachelor's degree by January 2020 or later. Current college students are eligible if they will earn their first degree by September 2027. Within the eligibility window, KHS does not give preference based on recency of the degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military service extension to degree-date eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For applicants who served in the military, KHS extends the eligibility window by two years; you must have earned your degree in January 2018 or later to enroll in 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This acknowledges longer service commitments; applicants claiming this extension should be prepared to document military service per program instructions (explicit documentation guidance is not provided on this page).

rubrics_metrics.name: No preference within the degree-date window
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the eligibility window, KHS does not give preference based on recency of the degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with degrees earned earlier in the window are not disadvantaged compared to more recent graduates.

rubrics_metrics.name: International applicants: degree equivalency and graduate program requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If you graduated from an institution outside the U.S., to be eligible for graduate study at Stanford you must meet the requirements of the graduate program(s) you wish to pursue and hold the equivalent of a U.S. bachelor's degree from a college or university of recognized standing. The Office of Graduate Admissions (not KHS) sets these policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with international degrees should consult Stanford's guidelines for minimum level of study for international applicants and contact the Office of Graduate Admissions for equivalency determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicants whose first/bachelor's degree was earned before the window
rubrics_metrics.description: If you earned your first/bachelor's degree more than seven years before your intended enrollment date (in 2019 or earlier, for the autumn 2027 intake), then you are not eligible for consideration as a Knight-Hennessy scholar, even if you have earned an additional degree in 2020 or later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such applicants may still apply to Stanford graduate programs and pursue other funding opportunities at Stanford; having a later graduate degree does not reset the 'first degree' date for KHS eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undocumented / DACA applicants eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have been granted DACA status, do not hold formal citizenship in any country, or are otherwise undocumented, you are eligible to apply for graduate study and matriculate at Stanford University and Knight-Hennessy Scholars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants in these circumstances are directed to Stanford's 'Undocumented at Stanford' resources for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicants who already hold a graduate degree
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have earned a graduate degree, you remain eligible to enroll as a Knight-Hennessy scholar in 2027 as long as you earned your first/bachelor's degree in 2020 or later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Having a graduate degree does not by itself disqualify an applicant; the relevant cutoff is the date of the first/bachelor's degree (with military exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrolled Stanford graduate students — timing rules and adding degrees
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are an enrolled Stanford graduate student: a Stanford PhD student who will start your PhD in 2026 may apply to KHS in 2026 to start KHS in 2027 (your second year). Otherwise, if you enrolled in a graduate degree program at Stanford in 2025 or earlier, you are not eligible for consideration as a Knight-Hennessy scholar for your current degree program. If you intend to apply to an additional degree program at the university, review the specific eligibility pathways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current students who wish to apply must ensure their timing aligns with the cohort start year and may need to apply to a new degree program or defer enrollment to match KHS start-year requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applying when you have deferred Stanford enrollment
rubrics_metrics.description: If you defer enrollment to a Stanford graduate program, you may apply to start as a Knight-Hennessy scholar for the year that you enroll in that graduate program as long as you continue to meet all other KHS eligibility requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided: if admitted to MBA and deferred enrollment to September 2027, you may apply in 2026 to enroll as a KHS in 2027. Ensure continued satisfaction of all KHS requirements at application time.

rubrics_metrics.name: No deferral of Knight-Hennessy Scholar offers
rubrics_metrics.description: Knight-Hennessy Scholars does not defer scholar offers. If you are selected as a Knight-Hennessy scholar and are unable to enroll, you must reapply for admission for the year you intend to enroll. Deferral of enrollment to a graduate program is handled by that department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates should plan to enroll in the cohort year if they accept a KHS offer; inability to enroll requires reapplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination with other fellowships — permitted and prohibited awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain awards may or may not be combined with KHS. (Page provides a list; 'Awards marked "No" may not be combined with KHS and may not be discontinued in order to apply to KHS.')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must check the specific awards list and note which fellowships are incompatible with KHS; awards marked 'No' cannot be combined with KHS and cannot be dropped solely to become eligible for KHS.
